newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most shares drop on Beirut Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: Most shares drop on Beirut Stock Exchange.

text.p: Most shares fell in a dull market on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Monday.
The LIBX bank index dropped 1.52 percent to 190.40 and the LISPI fell 0.59 percent to 96.30 while the BLOM general index fell 0.84 percent to 1103.92.
Shares were last traded on the BSE on Thursday because Friday was a public holiday.
BSE turnover climbed to 237,687 from 169,103 for a value of $3,447,192 against $1,367,621.
The turnover included a block trade of 24,000 Banque Audi shares outside the floor at $27.1250. Audi shares held steady at Thursday's $27.125.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce dropped to $20.5 from $21 and Bank of Beirut also fell to $5.6250 from $5.75.
Solidere A shares fell to $12.8750 from $13 and B shares dropped to $13 from $13.125.
"It is a dull market. We were expecting it to be this way in August. The big players are on vacation," said one broker.
There was no trade in the four listed industrial firms -- Ciments Libanais, Eternit, Ciments Blancs and and Uniceramic.
